sanskrit: pitāmaho hi gāṅgeyaḥ śaṃtanor adhi bhārata brahmarṣisadṛśo jajñe devair api durutsahaḥ pitrā hy uktaḥ prasannena nākāmas tvaṃ mariṣyasi
english: For the grandsire Bhīṣma, son of Gaṅgā, born of Śaṃtanu, O Bhārata, was born equal to a brahmarishi and even the gods find him hard to overcome. His pleased father told him: "You shall not die against your will."

sanskrit: brahmarṣeś ca bharadvājād droṇyāṃ droṇo vyajāyata droṇāj jajñe mahārāja drauṇiś ca paramāstravit
english: And Droṇa was born of the brahmarishi Bharadvāja, from the vessel called Droni. From Droṇa in turn was born Aśvatthāman, O great king, who is supreme in knowledge of weapons.

sanskrit: kṛpaś cācāryamukhyo 'yaṃ maharṣer gautamād api śarastambodbhavaḥ śrīmān avadhya iti me matiḥ
english: And Kṛpa, foremost among teachers, was born from the great sage Gautama, having sprung from a clump of reeds. He is glorious, and in my judgment he is invincible.

sanskrit: ayonijaṃ trayaṃ hy etat pitā mātā ca mātulaḥ aśvatthāmno mahārāja sa ca śūraḥ sthito mama
english: These three — father, mother, and maternal uncle — were not born of a womb, O great king. Aśvatthāman too is a hero, and he stands on my side.

sanskrit: sarva ete mahārāja devakalpā mahārathāḥ śakrasyāpi vyathāṃ kuryuḥ saṃyuge bharatarṣabha
english: All of these, O great king, are great chariot-warriors equal to the gods; in battle they would cause even Indra distress, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇakṛpāṇāṃ ca tulyaḥ karṇo mato mama anujñātaś ca rāmeṇa matsamo 'sīti bhārata
english: Karṇa I consider equal to Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Kṛpa. And Paraśurāma sanctioned him saying, "You are my equal," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kuṇḍale rucire cāstāṃ karṇasya sahaje śubhe te śacyarthe mahendreṇa yācitaḥ sa paraṃtapaḥ amoghayā mahārāja śaktyā paramabhīmayā
english: Karṇa had two beautiful, auspicious, natural earrings. He, the scorcher of foes, was asked by great Indra for them on behalf of Śacī, O great king, and was given instead an infallible, supremely terrible spear.

sanskrit: tasya śaktyopagūḍhasya kasmāj jīved dhanaṃjayaḥ vijayo me dhruvaṃ rājan phalaṃ pāṇāv ivāhitam abhivyaktaḥ pareṣāṃ ca kṛtsno bhuvi parājayaḥ
english: How could Dhanañjaya survive once that spear is employed against him? Victory is certain for me, O king, like a fruit already placed in hand; and the complete defeat of the enemy on this earth is manifest.

sanskrit: ahnā hy ekena bhīṣmo 'yam ayutaṃ hanti bhārata tat samāś ca maheṣvāsā droṇadrauṇikṛpā api
english: In a single day Bhīṣma slays ten thousand warriors, O Bhārata. And Droṇa, Aśvatthāman, and Kṛpa are equal to him in their prowess as great bowmen.

sanskrit: saṃśaptāni ca vṛndāni kṣatriyāṇāṃ paraṃtapa arjunaṃ vayam asmān vā dhanaṃjaya iti sma ha
english: And bands of sworn warriors among the kshatriyas, O scorcher of foes, have taken the oath: "Either Arjuna or we" — so shall Dhanañjaya meet them.

sanskrit: tāṃś cālam iti manyante savyasācivadhe vibho pārthivāḥ sa bhavān rājann akasmād vyathate katham
english: The kings consider these warriors sufficient for the slaying of Savyasācin. O lord, why then, O king, do you suddenly feel distress?

sanskrit: bhīmasene ca nihate ko 'nyo yudhyeta bhārata pareṣāṃ tan mamācakṣva yadi vettha paraṃtapa
english: If Bhīmasena is slain, who else among the enemy would fight? Tell me that, O Bhārata, if you know it, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: pañca te bhrātaraḥ sarve dhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha sātyakiḥ pareṣāṃ sapta ye rājan yodhāḥ paramakaṃ balam
english: Your five brothers, then Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and Sātyaki — these seven warriors of the enemy, O king, constitute their supreme strength.

sanskrit: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādayaḥ drauṇir vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ somadatto 'tha bāhlikaḥ
english: On our side the distinguished ones are Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa and others; Aśvatthāman, Karṇa son of the charioteer, Somadatta, and Bāhlika.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣādhipaḥ śalya āvantyo 'tha jayadrathaḥ duḥśāsano durmukhaś ca duḥsahaś ca viśāṃ pate
english: The lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, Śalya, the king of Avanti, Jayadratha, Duḥśāsana, Durmukha, and Duhsaha, O lord of men.

sanskrit: śrutāyuś citrasenaś ca purumitro viviṃśatiḥ śalo bhūriśravāś cobhau vikarṇaś ca tavātmajaḥ
english: Śrutāyus, Citrasena, Purumitra, Vivingsati, Śala, both Bhūriśravas, and Vikarṇa — your own son.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo hi me rājan daśaikā ca samāhṛtāḥ nyūnāḥ pareṣāṃ saptaiva kasmān me syāt parājayaḥ
english: I have assembled eleven akshauhinis, O king, while the enemy has only seven — how then could I be defeated?

sanskrit: balaṃ triguṇato hīnaṃ yodhyaṃ prāha bṛhaspatiḥ parebhyas triguṇā ceyaṃ mama rājann anīkinī
english: Bṛhaspati has said that a force three times weaker may still be fought. My army, O king, is three times greater than the enemy's.

sanskrit: guṇahīnaṃ pareṣāṃ ca bahu paśyāmi bhārata guṇodayaṃ bahuguṇam ātmanaś ca viśāṃ pate
english: I see many deficiencies in the enemy, O Bhārata, and I see many virtues and abundant merits on my own side, O lord of men.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ samājñāya balāgryaṃ mama bhārata nyūnatāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca na mohaṃ gantum arhasi
english: Having assessed all this — my supreme strength, O Bhārata, and the weakness of the Pāṇḍavas — you ought not to fall into delusion.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā saṃjayaṃ bhūyaḥ paryapṛcchata bhārata vidhitsuḥ prāptakālāni jñātvā parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, O Bhārata, he who was the conqueror of enemy cities, wishing to know what was timely and understanding the moment, questioned Sañjaya further.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca akṣauhiṇīḥ sapta labdhvā rājabhiḥ saha saṃjaya kiṃ svid icchati kaunteyo yuddhaprepsur yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Duryodhana said: Having obtained seven akshauhinis together with allied kings, O Sañjaya, what does Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, who is eager for battle, intend?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atīva mudito rājan yuddhaprepsur yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenārjunau cobhau yamāv api na bibhyataḥ
english: Sañjaya said: Yudhiṣṭhira is exceedingly joyful, O king, and eager for war. Both Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and even the twins, feel no fear.

sanskrit: rathaṃ tu divyaṃ kaunteyaḥ sarvā vibhrājayan diśaḥ mantraṃ jijñāsamānaḥ san bībhatsuḥ samayojayat
english: Arjuna, son of Kuntī, illuminating all directions, yoked his divine chariot, and Bībhatsu, wishing to recite his mantras, did so.

sanskrit: tam apaśyāma saṃnaddhaṃ meghaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ yathā sa mantrān samabhidhyāya hṛṣyamāṇo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: We saw him arrayed, shining like a lightning-lit cloud. After meditating upon his mantras, filled with joy, he spoke thus.

sanskrit: pūrvarūpam idaṃ paśya vayaṃ jeṣyāma saṃjaya bībhatsur māṃ yathovāca tathāvaimy aham apy uta
english: "See this as a good omen — we shall be victorious, O Sañjaya." Whatever Bībhatsu said to me, I find it to be true as well.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca praśaṃsasy abhinandaṃs tān pārthān akṣaparājitān arjunasya rathe brūhi katham aśvāḥ kathaṃ dhvajaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: You praise and glorify those sons of Pṛthā who were defeated at dice. Tell me about the horses on Arjuna's chariot, and about his banner.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhauvanaḥ saha śakreṇa bahucitraṃ viśāṃ pate rūpāṇi kalpayām āsa tvaṣṭā dhātrā sahābhibho
english: Sañjaya said: Viśvakarmā, the son of Bhuvana, together with Indra, O lord of men, fashioned many wondrous forms, as did Tvaṣṭṛ together with Dhata, O lord.

sanskrit: dhvaje hi tasmin rūpāṇi cakrus te devamāyayā mahādhanāni divyāni mahānti ca laghūni ca
english: On that banner they placed forms through divine illusion — forms of great value, celestial, both large and small.

sanskrit: sarvā diśo yojanamātram antaraṃ; sa tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca rurodha vai dhvajaḥ na saṃsajjet tarubhiḥ saṃvṛto 'pi; tathā hi māyā vihitā bhauvanena
english: That banner blocked all directions to a distance of a yojana, horizontally and upward; yet it would not catch on trees even when surrounded by them — such was the illusion arranged by the son of Bhuvana.

sanskrit: yathākāśe śakradhanuḥ prakāśate; na caikavarṇaṃ na ca vidma kiṃ nu tat tathā dhvajo vihito bhauvanena; bahvākāraṃ dṛśyate rūpam asya
english: Just as Indra's rainbow shines in the sky — not one color, and we cannot tell what it is — so too the banner fashioned by the son of Bhuvana: its form appears in many shapes.

sanskrit: yathāgnidhūmo divam eti ruddhvā; varṇān bibhrat taijasaṃ tac charīram tathā dhvajo vihito bhauvanena; na ced bhāro bhavitā nota rodhaḥ
english: Just as smoke from fire rises filling the sky, bearing luminous hues in its fiery body, so too the banner fashioned by the son of Bhuvana — it would be no burden and would cause no obstruction.

sanskrit: śvetās tasmin vātavegāḥ sadaśvā; divyā yuktāś citrarathena dattāḥ śataṃ yat tat pūryate nityakālaṃ; hataṃ hataṃ dattavaraṃ purastāt
english: White horses swift as the wind, noble and divine, given by Citraratha, were yoked to it. Whenever they fell they were replaced — such was the boon granted beforehand.

sanskrit: tathā rājño dantavarṇā bṛhanto; rathe yuktā bhānti tadvīryatulyāḥ ṛśyaprakhyā bhīmasenasya vāhā; raṇe vāyos tulyavegā babhūvuḥ
english: Similarly, the king's horses, ivory-colored and large, yoked to the chariot, shine forth, equal to him in valor. Bhīmasena's steeds, resembling spotted deer, were equal in speed to the wind in battle.

sanskrit: kalmāṣāṅgās tittiricitrapṛṣṭhā; bhrātrā dattāḥ prīyatā phalgunena bhrātur vīrasya svais turaṃgair viśiṣṭā; mudā yuktāḥ sahadevaṃ vahanti
english: Dapple-bodied horses with partridge-speckled backs, given joyfully by his brother Phalguna, superior to his heroic brother's own horses, were joyfully yoked and carried Sahadeva.

sanskrit: mādrīputraṃ nakulaṃ tv ājamīḍhaṃ; mahendradattā harayo vājimukhyāḥ samā vāyor balavantas tarasvino; vahanti vīraṃ vṛtraśatruṃ yathendram
english: Nakula, son of Mādrī, of the Ajamīḍha lineage, was carried by tawny horses, foremost of steeds, given by great Indra — powerful as the wind in speed — carrying the hero like Indra slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tulyāś caibhir vayasā vikrameṇa; javena caivāpratirūpāḥ sadaśvāḥ saubhadrādīn draupadeyān kumārān; vahanty aśvā devadattā bṛhantaḥ
english: Horses equal to these in age, valor, and speed — unmatched, noble steeds, large and god-given — carry the young princes, Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadī.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kāṃs tatra saṃjayāpaśyaḥ pratyarthena samāgatān ye yotsyante pāṇḍavārthe putrasya mama vāhinīm
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Whom did you see there, O Sañjaya, who had come as allies to fight the army of my son on behalf of the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca mukhyam andhakavṛṣṇīnām apaśyaṃ kṛṣṇam āgatam cekitānaṃ ca tatraiva yuyudhānaṃ ca sātyakim
english: Sañjaya said: I saw the foremost of the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, Kṛṣṇa, who had arrived; and there also Cekitāna and Yuyudhāna the Sātyaki.

sanskrit: pṛthag akṣauhiṇībhyāṃ tau pāṇḍavān abhisaṃśritau mahārathau samākhyātāv ubhau puruṣamāninau
english: These two great chariot-warriors, each with separate akshauhinis, had joined the Pāṇḍavas. Both are renowned and consider themselves great men.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyātha pāñcālyo daśabhis tanayair vṛtaḥ satyajitpramukhair vīrair dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamaiḥ
english: Then the Pāñcāla king with an akshauhini, surrounded by his ten sons with Satyajit at their head, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna as their leader.

sanskrit: drupado vardhayan mānaṃ śikhaṇḍiparipālitaḥ upāyāt sarvasainyānāṃ praticchādya tadā vapuḥ
english: Drupada, enhancing his glory, protected by Śikhaṇḍī, advanced, at that time overwhelming the body of all the armies.

sanskrit: virāṭaḥ saha putrābhyāṃ śaṅkhenaivottareṇa ca sūryadattādibhir vīrair madirāśvapurogamaiḥ
english: Virāṭa together with his two sons Śaṅkha and Uttara, and with heroes led by Suryadatta, with Madirāśva at their head.

sanskrit: sahitaḥ pṛthivīpālo bhrātṛbhis tanayais tathā akṣauhiṇyaiva sainyasya vṛtaḥ pārthaṃ samāśritaḥ
english: That guardian of the earth, together with his brothers and sons, surrounded by a full akshauhini of soldiers, had joined Pārtha's side.

sanskrit: jārāsaṃdhir māgadhaś ca dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cedirāṭ pṛthak pṛthag anuprāptau pṛthag akṣauhiṇīvṛtau
english: Jarasandhi of Magadha and Dhṛṣṭaketu king of the Cedis had arrived separately, each surrounded by separate akshauhinis.

sanskrit: kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca sarve lohitakadhvajāḥ akṣauhiṇīparivṛtāḥ pāṇḍavān abhisaṃśritāḥ
english: The five brothers of Kekaya, all bearing crimson banners, surrounded by an akshauhini, had joined the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: etān etāvatas tatra yān apaśyaṃ samāgatān ye pāṇḍavārthe yotsyanti dhārtarāṣṭrasya vāhinīm
english: These and so many others I saw assembled there, who will fight the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son on behalf of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yo veda mānuṣaṃ vyūhaṃ daivaṃ gāndharvam āsuram sa tasya senāpramukhe dhṛṣṭadyumno mahāmanāḥ
english: He who knows the human battle-array, the divine, the gandharva, and the demonic — that great-minded Dhṛṣṭadyumna stands at the head of their army.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo rājan bhāgaḥ kḷptaḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ taṃ virāṭo 'nu saṃyātā saha matsyaiḥ prahāribhiḥ
english: Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, O king, has been assigned as the portion of Śikhaṇḍī. Virāṭa with the Matsyas, who are fierce fighters, shall follow in that battle.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhasya pāṇḍuputrasya bhāgo madrādhipo balī tau tu tatrābruvan ke cid viṣamau no matāv iti
english: The powerful lord of the Madras was assigned as the portion of the eldest son of Pāṇḍu. But some of them said there: "The two of them seem unequal to us."

sanskrit: duryodhanaḥ sahasutaḥ sārdhaṃ bhrātṛśatena ca prācyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca bhīmasenasya bhāgataḥ
english: Duryodhana with his hundred sons, along with his hundred brothers, and the eastern and southern kings — these were assigned as the portion of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: arjunasya tu bhāgena karṇo vaikartano mataḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saindhavaś ca jayadrathaḥ
english: As Arjuna's appointed portion: Karṇa the son of the charioteer, Aśvatthāman, Vikarṇa, and Jayadratha the king of Sindhu.

sanskrit: aśakyāś caiva ye ke cit pṛthivyāṃ śūramāninaḥ sarvāṃs tān arjunaḥ pārthaḥ kalpayām āsa bhāgataḥ
english: And whoever on earth considers himself a hero and is difficult to overcome — all of them Arjuna, son of Pṛthā, has assigned as his own portion.

sanskrit: maheṣvāsā rājaputrā bhrātaraḥ pañca kekayāḥ kekayān eva bhāgena kṛtvā yotsyanti saṃyuge
english: The five brothers, princes of Kekaya, great bowmen, have designated the Kekayas as their own portion and will fight them in battle.

sanskrit: teṣām eva kṛto bhāgo mālavāḥ śālvakekayāḥ trigartānāṃ ca dvau mukhyau yau tau saṃśaptakāv iti
english: Their assigned portion also includes the Mālavas and the Śālva-Kekayas, and the two chief leaders of the Trigartas who are known as the sworn warriors.

sanskrit: duryodhanasutāḥ sarve tathā duḥśāsanasya ca saubhadreṇa kṛto bhāgo rājā caiva bṛhadbalaḥ
english: All the sons of Duryodhana, and likewise those of Duḥśāsana, and also king Bṛhadbala — these were assigned as the portion of Abhimanyu, son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: draupadeyā maheṣvāsāḥ suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhā droṇam abhiyāsyanti bhārata
english: The sons of Draupadī, great bowmen bearing banners adorned with gold, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, will march against Droṇa, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: cekitānaḥ somadattaṃ dvairathe yoddhum icchati bhojaṃ tu kṛtavarmāṇaṃ yuyudhāno yuyutsati
english: Cekitāna desires to fight Somadatta in single-chariot combat. And Yuyudhāna desires to fight the Bhoja, Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu mādreyaḥ śūraḥ saṃkrandano yudhi svam aṃśaṃ kalpayām āsa śyālaṃ te subalātmajam
english: Sahadeva, son of Mādrī, a hero who makes enemies cry out in battle, assigned as his own portion your brother-in-law, the son of Subala.

sanskrit: ulūkaṃ cāpi kaitavyaṃ ye ca sārasvatā gaṇāḥ nakulaḥ kalpayām āsa bhāgaṃ mādravatīsutaḥ
english: Ulūka the son of the gambler, and the tribes of the Sārasvata region — Nakula, son of Mādravatī, assigned these as his portion.

sanskrit: ye cānye pārthivā rājan pratyudyāsyanti saṃyuge samāhvānena tāṃś cāpi pāṇḍuputrā akalpayan
english: Whatever other kings, O king, shall march forth in battle to face them — the sons of Pāṇḍu have by challenge assigned those as well.

sanskrit: evam eṣām anīkāni pravibhaktāni bhāgaśaḥ yat te kāryaṃ saputrasya kriyatāṃ tad akālikam
english: Thus their armies have been divided into portions. Whatever needs to be done regarding you and your sons, let it be done without delay.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca na santi sarve putrā me mūḍhā durdyūtadevinaḥ yeṣāṃ yuddhaṃ balavatā bhīmena raṇamūrdhani
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: All my sons are fools, addicted to crooked gambling — those whose battle with the mighty Bhīma will come at the forefront of the fight.

sanskrit: rājānaḥ pārthivāḥ sarve prokṣitāḥ kāladharmaṇā gāṇḍīvāgniṃ pravekṣyanti pataṅgā iva pāvakam
english: All the kings, all those rulers of earth, already sprinkled by the law of Time, will enter the fire of the Gāṇḍīva bow like moths entering a flame.

sanskrit: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ manye kṛtavairair mahātmabhiḥ tāṃ raṇe ke 'nuyāsyanti prabhagnāṃ pāṇḍavair yudhi
english: I believe the army will be scattered by those great-souled ones who have been made into enemies. Who will follow it in battle once it has been shattered by the Pāṇḍavas in war?

sanskrit: sarve hy atirathāḥ śūrāḥ kīrtimantaḥ pratāpinaḥ sūryapāvakayos tulyās tejasā samitiṃjayāḥ
english: For they are all atirathas — great warriors, heroes, glorious, blazing with energy — equal in brilliance to the sun and fire, conquerors in battle.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhiro netā goptā ca madhusūdanaḥ yodhau ca pāṇḍavau vīrau savyasācivṛkodarau
english: Whose leader is Yudhiṣṭhira and whose protector is the slayer of Madhu, and whose warriors are the two heroic Pāṇḍavas Savyasācin and Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ sātyakir drupadaś caiva dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cātmajaḥ
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, and Sātyaki, and Drupada, and the son of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: uttamaujāś ca pāñcālyo yudhāmanyuś ca durjayaḥ śikhaṇḍī kṣatradevaś ca tathā vairāṭir uttaraḥ
english: And Uttamaujas the Pāñcāla, and the unconquerable Yudhāmanyu, and Śikhaṇḍī, and Kṣatradeva, and Uttara son of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: kāśayaś cedayaś caiva matsyāḥ sarve ca sṛñjayāḥ virāṭaputro babhrūś ca pāñcālāś ca prabhadrakāḥ
english: The Kāśis and the Cedis, all the Matsyas and all the Sṛñjayas, and Babhru son of Virāṭa, and the Pāñcālas and the Prabhadrakas.

sanskrit: yeṣām indro 'py akāmānāṃ na haret pṛthivīm imām vīrāṇāṃ raṇadhīrāṇāṃ ye bhindyuḥ parvatān api
english: From whom not even Indra could wrest this earth against their will — those heroes, steadfast in battle, who could cleave even mountains.

sanskrit: tān sarvān guṇasaṃpannān amanuṣyapratāpinaḥ krośato mama duṣputro yoddhum icchati saṃjaya
english: Against all these, endowed with virtues, blazing with superhuman energy, my wicked son, while I cry out, desires to fight, O Sañjaya.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ubhau sva ekajātīyau tathobhau bhūmigocarau atha kasmāt pāṇḍavānām ekato manyase jayam
english: Duryodhana said: Both sides are of the same birth, and both move on the same earth. Why then do you consider victory to rest on the side of the Pāṇḍavas alone?

sanskrit: pitāmahaṃ ca droṇaṃ ca kṛpaṃ karṇaṃ ca durjayam jayadrathaṃ somadattam aśvatthāmānam eva ca
english: The grandsire and Droṇa, and Kṛpa, and the unconquerable Karṇa, and Jayadratha, Somadatta, and Aśvatthāman —

sanskrit: sucetaso maheṣvāsān indro 'pi sahito 'maraiḥ aśaktaḥ samare jetuṃ kiṃ punas tāta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: — wise-minded great bowmen whom even Indra together with the immortals is unable to conquer in battle — how then can the Pāṇḍavas, O father?

sanskrit: sarvā ca pṛthivī sṛṣṭā madarthe tāta pāṇḍavān āryān dhṛtimataḥ śūrān agnikalpān prabādhitum
english: And all this earth has been created for my sake, O father, to crush those noble, resolute, heroic, fire-like Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: na māmakān pāṇḍavās te samarthāḥ prativīkṣitum parākrānto hy ahaṃ pāṇḍūn saputrān yoddhum āhave
english: The Pāṇḍavas are not capable of looking upon my forces. I am fully prepared to fight the sons of Pāṇḍu together with their sons in battle.

sanskrit: matpriyaṃ pārthivāḥ sarve ye cikīrṣanti bhārata te tān āvārayiṣyanti aiṇeyān iva tantunā
english: All the kings who desire to do what pleases me, O Bhārata, will bind them as with a thread, like black deer.

sanskrit: mahatā rathavaṃśena śarajālaiś ca māmakaiḥ abhidrutā bhaviṣyanti pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Attacked by my great forces of chariots and by my nets of arrows, the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas will be overwhelmed.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca unmatta iva me putro vilapaty eṣa saṃjaya na hi śakto yudhā jetuṃ dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: My son raves like a madman, O Sañjaya. For he is not capable of conquering Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira in battle.
